title: A non-technician can still press Start on an approved line and record time
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have a new staff member for this test, staff member A, on the built-in Parts Manager role, with Time Clock on and Technician off, enrolled at the test location only, who can sign in.
  • Have a new service work order for this test, work order 1, at the test location, in Approved, led by nobody (no lead), with one approved line, line 1, that staff member A is not on.
custom_steps:
1. Sign out.
  2. Sign in as staff member A.
  3. Open work order 1.
  4. Press Start on line 1.
  5. Press Stop on line 1.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • You are signed out.

Step 2:

  • Staff member A is signed in.

Step 3:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 4:

  • The timer starts on line 1, as today.

Step 5:

  • The time is recorded.
  • Staff member A is added to line 1's labor, as today.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Technician Toggle", Confluence 977371146, version 17 (2 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 2 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11788, story SV-11881 (Story 3, Who appears on the technician lists)

  • S3-E3: “A person who is not a technician can still press Start on an approved line and record time, as today; doing so adds them to the line's labor as today.”
  • Out of Scope: “Clocking in on a job. Anyone with Time Clock on can still press Start on an approved line and record time, as today. Time sheets, the time sheet dialogs and Punch Clock Activities keep listing everyone with Time Clock on except the Office User and Time Clock User roles, as today.”
  • Key Decisions: “Technician also decides only who is offered, not who can be assigned or record time: assignment and clocking are checked as today.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Technician Toggle" (https://claude.ai/artifact/1fuPz8Y4xTg7Syq1mfmJ9R), version 1793629882-06f7, read 2 Nov 2026: page "6 Technician dropdowns on a work order" (board note; no picture)

The design's own words:

  • “Time sheets keep every Time Clock user: a Parts Manager can still clock in and record time. Part sales have no technician dropdown on screen, so nothing there looks different.”
